key_idea: A tournament is exactly a rooted tree where every non-champion picks one stronger player to lose to, and a player's game count is its number of children plus one for its own loss, so it is a min/max cost assignment with capacities.
sketch: Sort by skill. Each player except the strongest must be assigned a parent with higher skill at cost s_i xor s_j; parent j can take at most g_j - 1 children (g_j for the overall strongest, who never loses). Any such tree is schedulable by playing subtrees bottom-up, and g>=2 guarantees feasibility (a chain). Run min-cost max-flow on source -> loser (cap 1) -> winner (cost xor) -> sink (cap), once with costs and once negated for the maximum; the graph is a DAG so SPFA handles negative costs. About 5000 edges and 99 augmentations. Costs reach 100*2^30 so use 64-bit. Verified against exhaustive parent assignment for n<=6.
